## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The two companions and the forgotten request  (`#the-two-companions-and-the-forgotten-request`)

Cited ayat: 12:35-42

> **12:35** ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُا۟ ٱلْـَٔايَٰتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُۥ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ
>

### Claims

**c1** (12:35): After they had seen the signs, it occurred to them to imprison the young man of the story for a time.

**c2** (12:36): Two young men entered the prison with him; one said he saw himself pressing wine, and the other that he saw himself carrying bread on his head, from which birds were eating; they asked him to tell them the interpretation, for they saw him as one of those who do good.

**c3** (12:37): He said that no food provided for them would come before he had informed them of its interpretation; this, he said, was from what his Lord had taught him; and he had left the way of a people who do not believe in God and who deny the Hereafter.

**c4** (12:38): He said that he followed the way of his forefathers Ibrahim, Ishaq and Yaqub, that it was not for them to associate anything with God, and that this was from God's favour on them and on people, though most people are not thankful.

**c5** (12:39-40): Speaking to his companions in prison, he asked whether scattered lords were better, or God, the One who prevails; he said that what they worshipped besides Him were only names that they and their fathers had given, for which God had sent down no authority, and that judgement belongs to God alone.

**c6** (12:41): He gave the interpretation: one of them would serve wine to his lord, and the other would be crucified and the birds would eat from his head; the matter about which they asked was decided.

**c7** (12:42): He said to the one he thought would be saved that he should mention him to his lord; Satan caused a forgetting of the mention of his lord, and he remained in prison for several years.

### One-minute summary

The young man of the story was imprisoned for a time, and two young men entered the prison with him and told him their dreams [c1][c2]. He gave them the interpretation, and asked the one he thought would be saved to mention him, but Satan caused a forgetting, and he stayed in prison for several years [c6][c7].

### Complete story

After they had seen the signs, it occurred to them to imprison the young man of the story for a time [c1]. Two young men entered the prison with him; one said he saw himself pressing wine, and the other that he saw himself carrying bread on his head, from which birds were eating, and they asked him to tell them the interpretation [c2].

He said that no food provided for them would come before he had informed them of its interpretation, and that this was from what his Lord had taught him [c3]. He said he followed the way of his forefathers Ibrahim, Ishaq and Yaqub, and that it was not for them to associate anything with God [c4]. He asked his companions whether scattered lords were better, or God, the One who prevails, and said that judgement belongs to God alone [c5].

He gave the interpretation: one of them would serve wine to his lord, and the other would be crucified and the birds would eat from his head [c6]. He said to the one he thought would be saved that he should mention him to his lord; Satan caused a forgetting of the mention of his lord, and he remained in prison for several years [c7].

### Deep study

The prison scene has several movements: the dreams of the companions [c2], his speech about what his Lord taught him and about God alone [c3][c4][c5], and the interpretation with its sequel [c6][c7]. The reference of 'his lord' in 12:42 can be read in two ways, as the freed man's master or as the speaker's own Lord, and the draft keeps both [c7]. The length of the stay is given only as several years [c7].

### Kids mode

Two young men came into the prison with him and told him their dreams [c2]. He told them what the dreams meant [c6]. He asked the one who would be saved to mention him, but that man forgot, and he stayed in prison for several years [c7].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that he speaks to his companions of God alone before he gives the interpretation [c3][c5]. Another is that the request to be mentioned is followed by a long wait [c7].

### What the sources do not establish

- The verses in this event do not name the young man; the story that surrounds them does, and this record does not name him because these verses do not.
- The Quran does not name the two young men or say what they had done; it does not say who his lord is in 12:41.
- Not established: how long a time (12:35) was, how old he was when he was imprisoned, what the signs were that they had seen, or who they are who decided on the prison.
- The Arabic for several years does not give an exact number of years.
- The reference of his lord in 12:42 can be read in two ways, as noted in the text; the verse does not settle it.
